newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA STAY TOP AS REAL FALTER AT SANTANDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA STAY TOP AS REAL FALTER AT SANTANDER.

text.p: Barcelona stayed top of the Spanish first division on Sunday after Real Madrid could manage only a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander.

Barcelona's emphatic 5-1 win at Compostela on Saturday, which included two memorable goals from Brazilian striker Ronaldo, leaves coach Bobby Robson's side two points clear at the top with 17 points from seven games.
Two points back are Deportivo Coruna, who lead Real Madrid on goal difference.

Real were once again unconvincing in a scrappy game which looked set to end in a goalless draw until just 20 minutes from the end when Racing's Russian forward Vladimir Beschastnykh broke the offside trap down the right and flicked the ball over Real's German goalkeeper Bodo Illgner.
Shortly afterwards the referee surprisingly awarded a penalty against Racing for what seemed to be routine pushing in the area. Croatian striker Davor Suker equalised from the spot.
But Racing struck straight back when defender Gabriel Schurrer rose above a sea of heads to nod home a cross.
With just five minutes left Real's Montenegrin striker Predrag Mijatovic capitalised on another goalmouth scramble to make it 2-2.
Mijatovic blotted his copybook in the dying moments when he spat in the face of a defender in an off-the-ball incident which the referee failed to spot.
Deportivo had Brazilian midfielder Donato to thank for a last-gasp strike at Oviedo, the only goal of a poor game.
Betis are in fourth place after Saturday's 2-2 draw at champions Atletico Madrid, who slipped to sixth.
Real Sociedad moved up to fifth with a comfortable 3-0 win over newcomers Extremadura who have not won a single point in seven matches in the first division.
Another newly-promoted side, Hercules, have yet to add to the three points they collected in their opening game of the season, against Extremadura.
Hercules clocked up their sixth successive defeat despite having the better of a rain-affected game against Rayo Vallecano. They lost 2-1.
